we have developed a SpiNNaker board-level power estimation model and demonstrated that SpiNNaker can be used to simulate a quarter of a millions neurons in real time with a power consumption of 1W.
SpiNNaker is capable of simulating large-scale spiking neural networks with high efficiency and flexibility, in real-time.

SpiNNaker is capable of running large-scale, heterogeneous, real-time spiking neural networks; the power consumption is linearly proportional to the number of neurons, synapse and their firing rates; SpiNNaker can simulate 1.8B events/sec with 81M synapses, 250K neurons and 1.2K neurons/chip.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the power consumption of SpiNNaker, and the implications of this on the design and simulation of large scale neural networks.
developing and optimising the power and performance of the SpiNNaker architecture for real-time neural network simulations.
understanding the power consumption of large-scale, heterogeneous, spiking neural network simulations on the SpiNNaker architecture.

we have shown that the SpiNNaker architecture is capable of simulating large-scale, complex spiking neural networks, in real-time, with a high degree of power efficiency, whilst maintaining a high degree of flexibility and programmability.

SpiNNaker is a powerful and flexible architecture for real-time simulation of large-scale spiking neural networks, with a power consumption per neuron that is at least an order of magnitude less than that of a conventional supercomputer.
SpiNNaker can simulate a quarter of a billion neurons, 81 billion synapses and 18 billion synaptic events per chip per second, consuming less than 0.8 W per chip.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SpiNNaker is a highly efficient architecture for simulating large-scale spiking neural networks in real-time, which is capable of running complex simulations on a single SpiNNaker chip.
the SpiNNaker architecture is capable of simulating large-scale, real time neural networks with low power consumption, which is a desirable characteristic in the context of neuromorphic engineering.

SpiNNaker is able to simulate large-scale, complex spiking neural networks with high efficiency and power consumption, whilst also offering flexibility to simulate a range of different neural network topologies and configurations.

, for large-scale neural networks, SpiNNaker can provide real-time performance at a fraction of the cost and energy consumption of alternative approaches.

, for the first time, a power model is available for SpiNNaker, which allows the user to predict the power consumption of a given neural network model on SpiNNaker, and to compare this to other architectures.
